scope: Current 716-strip full bench with separately approved six-pad support revision
reason: Current full-bench native Analyze returned normally with no rigid-mode message. Responses are withheld by independent kinematic review: four terminal strips retain free rotation about their point-pair lines. An empty native message is not a zero-mode certificate.
issues: Preliminary linear elastic response only; no grade, connection capacity, furniture-code or safety approval.
Geometry working scale is documented but physically unmeasured.
All 1264 contacts are proposed analytical connection locations; no independent fastener verification is claimed.
Pair tie points have 18mm geometric patch-edge inset and 24mm spacing; these do not verify grain-dependent screw end distances or a fastener product.
Four terminal mechanisms are deliberately retained; do not present native finite output as valid equilibrium if a mechanism is certified.
Six newly approved unanchored leveling pads are separate support items outside the preserved timber allocation.
Negative vertical reactions indicate uplift and invalidate the bilateral resting assumption; horizontal reactions are friction demands, not anchor capacities.
Offset arms use massless 1000x provisional elastic moduli, a numerical approximation rather than calibrated physical connector stiffness.

connections.summary: 1,264 actual broad-face patches grouped into four archetypes. The primary model has two ideal translation ties per patch, explicit member offsets, and a free relative rotation about each pair line. These are proposed connections, not 1,264 independently verified fasteners.

archetypes.title: Lower To Side
archetypes.translation: UX/UY/UZ tied at each of two separate face points.
archetypes.rotation: Two relative rotations restrained by pair geometry; rotation about point-pair line released.
archetypes.coordinate_system: Global XYZ; face lies in XZ, thickness normal Y. Pair-axis vector is recorded per contact.
archetypes.fastening_concept: Proposed paired through-face structural timber screws with clamping/bearing provision; screw specification and capacity unverified.
archetypes.assumption: Ideal translational ties and explicit massless offsets; no calibrated slip law and no independent fastener verification.

supports: Six unanchored levelled bearings at S005/S040/S075, B01+B09; support rotations free.
Actual lower-edge contacts sit on separate pads over working plane z=-15 mm.
UX/UY restraint at S005 B01 and UX at S075 B01 remove horizontal rigid motion; nonzero reactions require friction justification.
Negative Z reactions invalidate bilateral resting contact; no anchor capacity is assumed.
connections: Two-point tie gives five relative kinematic constraints; four one-overlap terminal strips retain rotational mechanisms.
Numerical offset modulus factors 1000 and 100 are sensitivity assumptions, not measured joint stiffness.

There are 3 rigid body modes in the system. This means some parts can move freely without causing deformation.
 Try to use the 'Eigen Modes'-component and activate the display of local coordinate axes: The first eigen-mode will be the rigid body motion.
 If this does not help, check whether you have a pinned support directly attached to a hinge. A hinge introduces an extra node which may cause the problem.
 When analyzing a flat shell structure one has to lock the rotation perpendicular to the plate in at least one node.
